Another week of freezing rain and cold, got my van back from the shop today and immediately treated it like a truck again, took a drive to the elusive Splake pond. Hoping to fish it before ice.

Shitty cold wet time of year, and I'm the local heating guy it's my busy season work wise. Just got my van back from the shop, I blew a CV axle in half, So the first thing I did was take it an hour north in the bushand treat it like a truck again just to see if my van can make it into the splake pond.

The weather is supposed to clear up a bit this week, cold but dry, so I'm hoping to hit this pond with the canoe a couple times before ice. I've only ever ice fished here, but I understand the lake, it has a deep 35 foot hole and almost dorectly in the middle is a sandbar thats only about 2ft deep and then there are 2 15-20ft holes on the opposite side of the sand bar, so for a small pond it has lots of character, I suspect the fish feed along the dropoff of the sandbar so that's going to be what I focus on, but they could also patrol the shoreline dropoff just as much.

*Splake are a hybrid of Brook and Lake Trout, none of which are really Trout but are actually Char

Oh and I saw a moose, but it was dead.

Splake are one of my favourite fish since there's no limit (size or number) in my zone. Just to add for anyone who doesn't know is that splake are infertile so that's why no limits exist since they crowd the lake and take resources from the brooks and lakers.

The pond must be fairly unknown or else it would be fished out I'm guessing?

I love splake too but they can be finicky to fish for with their genetic identity crisis and all, I also love that they grow big fast, we have limits but no seasons for stocked trout, 5 per person a day no slot sizes, this pond is 100% splake no competition.

This pond isn't so much unknown as it is far away from anything else, not many people want to drive an hour north of town(town is only 1500 people) down rough dirt road to fish for stocked splake we have a million other fishing opportunities closer to town and more accessible. There is another lake just behind this one with brooks and splake but it's quite the walk for me down an ATV trail with a canoe on my back and I like to take a deep cycle battery motor and fish finder etc....So ths pond will have to do.

But this whole area nothing ever gets fished out because there's no people here. I'm up in the Northwestern part of Ontario where people generally don't live.

The lake I normally fish used to have a lot of Americans (Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana etc) and it boggled my mind how they would keep 8 inch pickerel and 8 pound bass. Anything and everything to fill their tanks. I've only ever been stopped by a Conservation Officer once in my life and that was at a family cottage near Peterborough. Here they only patrol the river where there are Kings and Pinks so you'll never get caught for illegal fishing inland lake fishing.

What boggles the mind is how so many people don't understand that keeping fish outside the limits is going to hurt the ecosystem. It took long enough for them to figure out it wasn't beneficial taking the largest fish out. I remember as a kid I could never understand it as the bigger the bass the more eggs they have (fileting in season but sometimes the females still have eggs obviously). Anyways, one of our camps when I was growing up had the mouth netted during pickerel runs (Natives who legally could) and it only took two seasons before we didn't catch anymore pickerel. It was a good lesson for me to learn as it made me realize how important it was to respect nature. It's nice to hear that you understand this concept too as a lot of people don't get it.

Big fish don't even taste good, the meat gets soft and mushy.

As a Canadian I'm going to naturally assume pickerel = walleye, I get corrected by americans all the time and I'm sick of it, ya walleye isn't a pckerel techically a pickerel is like a little pike, but in canada it's a pickerel because we only have real pike.

Anyways I fish the same seasons white people can fish but my personal sizes for local fish are;

pretty much any trout over 11 inches, lake trout have to be under 22" big lake trout are too greasy, I don't even like fishing for lake trout because they live so deep. that's why I like splake, but you can't release anything from under 30ft deep or it's just going to die anyways from barotrauma.

Pickerel/Eyeballs I like them 15-20", I'll let anything bigger or smaller go unless it's slightly smaller and fat.

Yellow perch I'll keep anything over 8" we get them up to 14-16"

Pike, fuck I love me some pike, They are just as good as walleye once you take the bones out. I'll keep 28-36"

We don't really have much else this far north other then whitefish burbot, cisco and other herrings and suckers which I'll gladly keep whatever I catch and put on the smoker.

We get Salmon and rainbow trout runs in the spring and some sturgeon too, I've never fished the sturgeon but I'll take the salmon and rainbow, the salmon are just going to die anyways.

I think the neatest part of the pictures is that up north at the pond, there are no broadleaves left and there is snow on the ground, while closer to town the broadleaves havn't all fallen yet and there is no snow on the ground yet. It hasn't snowed in town in about a week but rained every day(which melts snow).

Beautiful area.
